A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARES research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original error-detection experiments on four datasets, controlled ClaimTrees analyses, best-of-N selection results, and PRM experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a scored ClaimTrees case study in Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same autoregressive Bernoulli sampling and Monte Carlo entailment estimation, followed by threshold-based error detection. Expanded scoring and prompting documentation does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PRMBench, DeltaBench, ClaimTrees, and CaptainCookRecipes, including the same chain-length, tree-width/depth, benign-error, and best-of-N scenarios. The new ClaimTrees example remains within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Entail-Prev/Base, ROSCOE, ReCEval, and LLM-Judge comparators. The Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B comparisons already appear in v1's Appendix C.8 and Table A7.

E3.justification: Metrics, model configurations, threshold selection, and five-fold evaluation remain unchanged. v2 specifies one fold for validation and four for testing; v1 did not specify this allocation, so this is additional documentation rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: New Table 2 illustrates an initial ClaimTrees error at Claim 7 and its propagation to Claim 8, comparing methods' step judgments. Existing sensitivity, robustness, and ablation analyses are retained, with detailed ablation discussion moved to Appendix C.8.

E5.justification: Five-fold means and standard deviations, best-of-N bootstrap uncertainty, and existing uncertainty values are retained. Appendix C.3's explicit statement about standard deviations across folds repeats information already provided in v1's experimental setup.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, sensitivity, best-of-N, PRM, and appendix ablation tables have identical numerical entries. New Table 2 reports ARES scores of 0.79, 0.82, 0.00, and 0.00 for Claims 5–8 alongside comparator judgments, adding case-level results rather than benchmark performance gains.

T1.justification: Definition 2.1 drops the explicit restriction to a deterministic entailment model while retaining the certainty condition. Equation (5) changes its left-hand index from 1:n+k to 1:n, introducing an inconsistency. Theorem 3.1 and its Appendix A proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain probabilistic autoregressive soundness certification and robust detection of propagated errors. The abstract retains the same headline results, including 72.1% Macro-F1 and 90.3% F1; rewritten passages preserve the overall scientific claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly qualifies the recommendation to include all base claims: its benefit on clear-cut ClaimTrees examples may differ under ambiguous entailment. It also explains that this choice avoids resampling and reduces variance. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds contradiction-score mappings, manual dataset-specific prompt-tuning details, explicit fold allocation, directions to prompt/package information, and an MIT-license statement. Hardware, spending, and default hyperparameters remain unchanged; the existing entailment Likert mapping is relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially reframes positioning around guarantees for single-step explanations versus multi-step reasoning. It adds broad coverage of interpretable models, attribution, recourse, Faithful Chain-of-Thought, and conformal generation, replacing the earlier emphasis on selected cross-domain applications of statistical guarantees.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion; reorganizes related work; and condenses the main-text ablations while retaining their detail in Appendix C.8. Affiliations and disclosure sections are updated, but the overall document organization and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ClaimTrees comparison table, relocates figures and appendix tables, and expands the best-of-N caption. Figure 5 has revised ticks and changes the CaptainCook4D label to CaptainCookRecipes. Existing diagrams and result-table structures are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The worked ClaimTrees comparison and clearer scoring, fold-allocation, prompting, and licensing documentation improve transparency, while the revised related work provides broader context. These are limited gains: the benchmark evidence and central guarantee are unchanged, and the new indexing inconsistency in Equation (5) is a local regression in mathematical clarity.
